title: Plasmonic Modes in hybrid Josephson Junction Arrays
authors: Alex Kirchner, Simon Feyrer, Vjeko Dimić, Johanna Berger, Davide Curcio, Giorgio Biasiol, Michael Prager, Matthias Kronseder, Dominique Bougeard, Nicola Paradiso, Christoph Strunk, Leandro Tosi
abstract: We present microwave characterization measurements of Josephson junction arrays (JJAs) based on epitaxial Al-InAs quantum well heterostructure. The Josephson inductance of the constituent planar junctions can be derived by probing the low-energy plasmon modes of these devices. Applying an out-of-plane magnetic field gives rise to a Fraunhofer-like diffraction pattern, from which the current-phase relation and the effective transparency can be extracted. JJAs can be used to achieve high inductances, suitable for the implementation of quantum circuits. They also provide an excellent test-bed for studying the microscopic excitations of hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices associated with the presence of Andreev states. Here, we demonstrate their tunability over a broad range of out-of-plane magnetic fields.
summary: This paper uses microwave spectroscopy to characterize Josephson Junction Arrays (JJAs) made from Al/InAs heterostructures. By measuring the plasmonic resonance frequency as a function of an out-of-plane magnetic field, the authors extract the Josephson inductance and the current-phase relation. This demonstrates the utility of JJAs as tunable testbeds for studying superconducting phenomena in hybrid quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the Josephson inductance and study the plasmonic modes of Josephson Junction Arrays (JJAs) fabricated on hybrid superconductor-semiconductor heterostructures.
main_result: The measurements successfully demonstrated the tunability of the Josephson inductance over a broad range of out-of-plane magnetic fields, allowing for the extraction of the current-phase relation (CPR) and effective transparency.
method: Microwave characterization measurements were performed by probing the low-energy plasmonic modes of the JJA, analyzing the resulting Fraunhofer-like diffraction patterns.
model_or_system: The physical system is a JJA built on an Al/InAs heterostructure, configured as the center conductor of a coplanar waveguide resonator. The analysis relies on fitting the magnetic field dependence of the resonance frequency to extract the Josephson inductance and CPR.
key_observables: Josephson inductance ($L_J$), plasmonic modes dispersion relation $\omega(k)$, and the Fraunhofer-like diffraction pattern of the resonance frequency.
important_parameters: Out-of-plane magnetic field ($B_{\perp}$), temperature ($T \approx 20 - 100 	ext{ mK}$), and the superconducting gap parameter ($\Delta^*N \approx 16 	ext{ meV}$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes $C_0/C_J = 2/3$ for dispersion relation calculations, and background subtraction is performed using reference measurements.
figures_summary: Figures show the device layout and circuit model, the plasmon dispersion relation, and microwave transmission traces illustrating the interference patterns (Fraunhofer patterns) for different devices at various magnetic fields.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of presenting the physical setup (JJA on Al/InAs), detailing the microwave measurement technique (probing plasmon modes), and then analyzing the magnetic field dependence of the resonance to extract fundamental superconducting parameters like $L_J$ and the CPR.
why_interesting: The work provides a direct experimental platform to probe the microscopic superconducting properties (like Andreev states) in semiconductor-superconductor interfaces using macroscopic circuit measurements (plasmon resonance), which is highly relevant for superconducting quantum circuit development.
